# Docs review instructions

Applies to shared rule files, skill docs, agent docs, `docs/` reference pages,
the README, `AGENTS.md`, and the Copilot review-instruction files. Conventions
come from `.ai-style-rules.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `rules/agent-guidelines.md`,
`skills/inherit-legacy-style/SKILL.md`, `README.md`, and the `docs/` pages
`skills.md`, `installers.md`, `models.md`, and `out-of-scope.md`.

## Shared rule files

- `rules/` is the single source of truth for rule text. Installed per-harness
  copies (an `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` managed block, `~/.claude/core-rules.md`)
  are generated by the installer and overwritten on every install. Flag a doc
  or script change that has anyone hand-edit an installed copy instead of
  editing `rules/` and reinstalling.
- `rules/core-rules.md` is a deliberate subset of `rules/agent-guidelines.md`,
  and each digest bullet is a deliberate compression of its counterpart, not
  a mirror. Flag a PR that re-adds a deliberately dropped rule to the digest
  on the assumption every rule should appear in both files, and flag a digest
  bullet that no longer names its rule's core obligation. Word-level parity
  is not expected.
- Pilot-before-scale and the PR-body heading set are skill-owned (carried by
  `plan-and-track` and `yeet`). Flag a PR that adds either to
  `rules/agent-guidelines.md` or `rules/core-rules.md`.

## Skill files

- Review a `SKILL.md` frontmatter `description` for routing first: it should
  front-load the user's intent, concrete trigger terms, and the nearest
  negative boundary rather than summarize, and keep clauses that prevent
  known misroutes. About 500 decoded characters is an informational target,
  not a cap; 1,024 is the format maximum.
- Frontmatter values are quoted only when YAML forces it, and the repo was
  audited as already following that. Flag a PR that migrates files to uniform
  quoting or uniform unquoting, and don't flag a value for being quoted or
  unquoted when YAML doesn't force the choice.
- A skill body takes one of three shapes. A checklist (like `plan-and-track`)
  uses H2 phase sections in execution order holding one imperative
  numbered step list with continuous numbering, a cross-cutting rules
  section first and a mode section last; `yeet` adds an unnumbered preamble and a closing `## Sources`.
  A reference skill (like `read-the-damn-docs`, `migration-discipline`) uses
  named reference H2s around one distinctly named procedure H2. A numbered
  reference (like `logging-practices`) numbers every H2, with one procedure
  (`## 9. Verify`) and a closing red-flags catalog. Flag a skill whose
  procedure is scattered with no named or numbered section to anchor it, a
  `## Prerequisites` section that isn't a real hard-stop dependency check,
  and a `## Sources` section in a body that asserts no live-observed
  third-party behavior.
- Detail a `SKILL.md` offloads lives in a flat `references/<kebab-name>.md`
  beside it. The SKILL.md keeps the condensed rule inline and closes that
  section with a markdown-link pointer (`Read [references/x.md](references/x.md)
  when/before <trigger>`). Flag a new pointer written as bare backticks, a
  new reference file that doesn't open with an H1 and a `Read this
  when/before ...` lead line, and one past about 100 lines with no
  `## Contents` list. Don't re-flag the existing `yeet` and
  `inherit-legacy-style` bare-backtick pointers, `publish-visual-pr`'s
  mid-section manifest pointer, or the existing reference files without a
  lead line, which are known defects.
- Cross-skill references in a skill body use `[[skill-name]]` wiki-link
  syntax instead of duplicating another skill's content.
- New skills default to portable across Claude, Codex, and Copilot. Flag a
  skill scoped to one harness whose PR doesn't say why, doesn't record the
  split in `docs/skills.md`, or adds an installer scope exception for a skill
  that could be portable.
- Flag a skill or rule that mandates an output convention (an owner tag, a
  required trailer, a section format) with no paired mechanical check, such
  as a hook lint or a CI assertion, since session attention alone doesn't
  hold a convention over a long run.
- A skill vendored from an external repo (`frontend-design`, `webapp-testing`)
  carries an HTML comment right after its frontmatter naming the source URL
  and the exact edits made (never "lightly edited"), with the upstream
  license verbatim in a sibling `LICENSE.txt`. A vendored section of an
  `agents/*.md` file carries the same comment above that section, with an
  `agents/<name>.LICENSE.txt`. Folding one vendored skill into another extends
  the surviving comment with a sentence naming the folded source. Flag a
  vendored file missing the comment or license text, a fold-in that drops the
  retired skill's provenance, and a vendored skill whose upstream license
  forbids redistribution (check the license text) instead of being fetched at
  install time the way `install-office-skills.sh` handles the
  `docx`/`pdf`/`pptx`/`xlsx` skills.
- A skill or rule rewritten from scratch but inspired by a public repo gets
  a one-line "adapted from" credit in `AGENTS.md`, in its Skills section for
  a skill or its rule-delivery section for a rule. Flag one merged without
  that credit. A source that is a private or employer-internal repository
  gets no credit anywhere, so don't flag its absence; flag a credit that
  names one.

## Subagent definition files

- An `agents/*.md` file has frontmatter in the order `name`, `description`,
  `model`, `effort`, `tools`. Its body is a short role statement, then a plain
  `How to work:` label (not a heading) over bold-lead principles. Flag a
  reordered or missing field and a `How to work` heading.
- `model` and `effort` pin in lockstep per role, not per model name:
  `fable`/`high` for `architect-reviewer`, `security-auditor`, and
  `fable-advisor`; `opus`/`xhigh` for `planner` (the only `xhigh`);
  `sonnet`/`high` for `researcher`, `debugger`, and `executor`;
  `haiku`/`medium` for `mechanic`. Flag a pair that departs from this.
- `tools` is a bare comma-separated subset that encodes authority:
  `Read, Grep, Glob` for read-only reviewers, advisors, and the planner;
  `researcher` adds `WebFetch, WebSearch`; `debugger` adds `Bash`
  (restricted to read-only in prose); `mechanic` adds `Edit, Write`;
  `executor` adds `Edit, Write, Bash`. Flag a reviewer, advisor, or planner
  granted write tools, and a tool grant that doesn't match the agent's
  documented authority in `docs/models.md`.
- `description` opens with the role and the tier rationale, naming the tier
  generically ("the roster's strongest-judgment tier"), never a model such as
  "Fable" or "Sonnet", then says when to delegate. The installer renders
  the same file into Codex TOML and a Copilot `.agent.md` that differ in
  whether `model` and `effort` appear, so prose naming a model goes stale on
  those harnesses. Flag a `description` with no trigger clause, with no
  inline tier rationale, or that names a model directly.

## Copilot review-instruction files

- They live at `.github/instructions/<bucket>.instructions.md`: a repo-wide
  `applyTo: "**"` bucket plus one per distinct area the sources evidence.
  Frontmatter sets `applyTo` and a mandatory `excludeAgent: "cloud-agent"`.
  The body is a one-line H1, a pointer to the sources backing the bucket
  instead of a restatement, then H2 sections of imperative "Flag ..."
  directives.
- A file carrying the `<!-- Generated by copilot-review-instructions; ... -->`
  marker is fully owned by that skill: flag a manual edit to one instead of
  changing its source and re-running the skill. A file without the marker
  might be hand-authored: flag it for the author to confirm provenance
  rather than treating the missing marker as settled.
- The skill also owns just the `# Code reviews` section of
  `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (marker as its first line, bounded by the
  heading through the next H1 or end of file). The rest of that file is
  hand-authored guidance that also steers Copilot's cloud agent. Flag an
  edit inside the marked section made without re-running the skill.

## Reference-doc structure

- `docs/*.md` and `README.md` use one H2 per component or topic, short
  paragraphs rather than run-on bullets, and one H3 per independent
  sub-behavior (`docs/hooks.md` gives each of `plan-gate.js`'s gates its own
  H3). A cross-cutting section (`## Shared script architecture`,
  `## Overview`) comes before the per-item ones, and a closed mapping or
  env-var-driven variance renders as a markdown table. Flag a doc edit that
  reverts to run-on bullets, folds several sub-behaviors into one paragraph,
  folds cross-cutting content into the first per-item section, or writes a
  closed mapping as prose. `.ai-style-rules.md` itself is exempt from this
  shape.
- Reference detail (per-harness tables, the subagent roster, per-hook
  behavior, installer rules) lives in `docs/*.md`, one topic per file, linked
  from the README or `AGENTS.md`. Flag a README or `AGENTS.md` section that
  has grown into a reference table or per-item enumeration, as a candidate
  for extraction to `docs/`.
- Use `-` as the bullet marker in doc prose (`docs/*.md`, `README.md`,
  `AGENTS.md`), never `*`, except inside a fenced block quoting external
  template text. Flag any other `*`-marked bullet outside a fence; don't
  re-flag `docs/tag-and-release.md`'s six-item pre-publish checklist, the one
  known exception.

## `.ai-style-rules.md` records current state

- Flag a dated entry, a `### [YYYY-MM-DD] Style Evolution Log` section, or
  "since the last round" / "was generalized to" narration inside a rule in
  `.ai-style-rules.md`. This repo is git-tracked, so per
  `skills/inherit-legacy-style/SKILL.md` (Incremental update, step 3) the file
  keeps no changelog: the commit that changes it is the change record.
- Flag a header or rule in `.ai-style-rules.md` written as the story of how it
  got there instead of the convention that holds now, and a header missing the
  commit fingerprint or scale tier or a file missing any of the Golden Files,
  Naming & State-Control Rules, or DONTs sections (`skills/inherit-legacy-style/SKILL.md`,
  First-time full scan, step 5).
- Flag a rule in `.ai-style-rules.md` that an instructions file (`AGENTS.md`,
  `rules/`) or a `docs/*.md` page already states. That owner keeps the rule,
  and the file points to it instead of restating it (same skill: step 5, and
  the Fold into docs fallback).

## Out-of-scope decisions

- `docs/out-of-scope.md` records a decision not to build something, so a
  later PR doesn't re-propose it. A decision about how an existing component
  behaves belongs in that component's own header, and a correction about how
  to work belongs in the gitignored `.tasks/lessons.md`. Flag an entry that is
  really one of those two.
- An entry there is a starting point for re-litigation, not a permanent ban.
  Flag a PR that reopens one without updating the entry, leaving it silently
  contradicted.

## Skimmable docs

- State results and decisions plainly. Flag a section inflated with
  exhaustive tuning detail that belongs in a script or SKILL.md header,
  content duplicated across sections, a table cell longer than one line, and
  dense nested bullets where plain prose would read better. The README is
  what, why, install, and where things live, not a complete reference.
